## Three countries in 12 days: when to choose Brazil, Argentina and Chile

This tour combines [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/), Iguazu Falls, [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/) and [Santiago de Chile](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/) without an expedition across Bolivia's highlands. In **12 days and 11 nights**, travellers experience the Atlantic coast, tropical waterfalls, tango and Chile's Pacific coastline. It is a busy sightseeing trip with several regional flights, but its geography is more compact than on four- or five-country itineraries.

Rather than moving to a different city every day, this itinerary leaves time for major attractions and independent exploration: three nights each in Rio, Buenos Aires and Santiago, and two nights at Iguazu.

## How the overnight stays are distributed and why it matters

| Stop | Nights |
|---|---:|
| Rio de Janeiro | 3 |
| Foz do Iguaçu | 2 |
| Buenos Aires | 3 |
| Santiago de Chile | 3 |

In [Rio](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/), separate excursions cover Corcovado and Christ the Redeemer, Sugarloaf Mountain and the city centre. Optional activities vary greatly: walking through old neighbourhoods, visiting the Botanical Garden, or taking a helicopter or hang-gliding flight. Choose these separately, taking account of each activity's duration and restrictions.

At [Iguazu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/), you visit the falls from **both countries**. On the Brazilian side, broad viewing platforms show the entire system; on the [Argentine side](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/), trails approach the water and Devil's Throat. Optional activities such as the Macuco Safari boat ride or Bird Park are not part of the main itinerary unless selected separately.

## What Buenos Aires adds after the nature section

[Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/) returns the journey to urban architecture, neighbourhoods and music. The included programme has a city tour and a tango show with dinner. A separate free day means visiting Argentina is more than a quick transit between flights.

Additional possibilities include Tigre, a gaucho ranch and an excursion to Uruguay. Their appearance in the optional list **does not mean they are included in the basic itinerary**. If Uruguay needs to be a third main country, consider the [13-day route with Colonia, Montevideo and Punta del Este](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-uruguay-13-days/).

## Santiago, Valparaíso and Viña del Mar

After flying to Chile, travellers tour [Santiago de Chile](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/). The itinerary also includes an excursion to [Valparaíso and Viña del Mar](/chile/place/valparaiso-vina-del-mar/) on the Pacific coast. This adds an important contrast: after humid tropical landscapes and capitals, travellers discover coastal cities with different architecture and climate.

Valparaíso has distinctive hillside neighbourhoods, a historic port and steep streets. Viña del Mar offers another type of urban environment on the same coastline. Plan clothing for central Chile's weather at the time of travel, not just for Rio.

A wine excursion to the Maipo Valley is available as an extra. **Wine tasting at a vineyard is not automatically included** in the main itinerary.

## What's included and where extra costs may arise

The price includes hotel accommodation, main **group excursions with Russian-speaking guides**, shared transfers with drivers, and regional flights **Rio–Iguazu–Buenos Aires–Santiago**. The Valparaíso visit is an exception to the general Russian-speaking guide arrangement, so confirm the language of guiding for that section before booking.

International flights, optional excursions, and food and drinks during transfers are excluded. Regional South American flights are already included on this itinerary, which makes it fundamentally different from some other Ada Tours programmes where these flights are paid separately.

Before booking, check the actual departure date from Santiago, the arrival time of your international flight and the order of excursions. Individual excursions may be rescheduled, but the list of compulsory visits should remain intact.

## Who this itinerary suits and when to add Peru

This tour suits travellers looking for **three distinct urban cultures, both sides of Iguazu and a short visit to the Pacific coast**, without a substantial high-altitude jeep expedition.

If you also want to see the [Sacred Valley of the Incas](/peru/place/sacred-valley-of-the-incas/) and [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/), compare the [15-day Brazil–Argentina–Chile–Peru tour](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-chile-peru-15-days/). It is longer, and its flights are charged separately, so compare the full list of services. For other combinations, see the [multi-country tour catalogue](/multi-country/).

## Frequently asked questions about the Brazil–Argentina–Chile tour

### Are flights between the cities included?

Yes. The Rio–Iguazu–Buenos Aires–Santiago flights are included in the programme. International flights cost extra.

### How much time is allocated to Iguazu?

Two nights in Foz do Iguaçu and excursions on both the Brazilian and Argentine sides. It is a substantial nature section, not a brief connection stop.

### Will there be a visit to a Chilean winery?

The Maipo Valley wine excursion is listed as optional. It must be booked separately to be included.

### Are all excursions guided in Russian?

Main group excursions have Russian-speaking guides, **except the Valparaíso trip**. Confirm the guiding language for that section.

## New Year 2027 in Brazil, Argentina and Chile: an 11-day journey

The main event of this itinerary happens right at the beginning: **the night of 31 December 2026 to 1 January 2027 in Rio de Janeiro**, on Copacabana beach. The trip then continues to Iguazu Falls, Buenos Aires and Santiago. The whole programme lasts **11 days and 10 nights**, from 30 December to 9 January.

This is a [group tour](/multi-country/) with Russian-speaking guides on the main excursions and flights between the cities included in the price. Its main appeal is celebrating New Year beside the ocean and then experiencing Argentina and Chile without having to piece together a series of regional flights independently.

## Four stops and the travel calendar

| Dates | Route location |
|---|---|
| 30 Dec–2 Jan | Rio de Janeiro |
| 3–4 Jan | Iguazu region |
| 5–6 Jan | Buenos Aires |
| 7–9 Jan | Santiago and departure |

The first four nights are scheduled in [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/). Arrival gives time to settle in before the festivities. On 31 December, the itinerary visits Christ the Redeemer on Corcovado, while the evening is devoted to New Year. On the following day, it includes Sugarloaf Mountain and the historic centre; 2 January is free.

On 3 January, the group flies to [Foz do Iguaçu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/). The Brazilian side of the waterfalls is visited on 4 January, followed by the Argentine side on 5 January and a flight to Buenos Aires after the excursion. On 6 January, there is a capital city tour and a tango show with dinner. The final days involve flying to Chile and discovering [Santiago](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/).

## New Year's Eve on Copacabana: included and optional elements

New Year's Eve on Copacabana is associated with large celebrations by the ocean: music, white clothing, traditional offerings to Iemanjá and midnight fireworks. This evening is the central event of the tour. The daytime Corcovado excursion lets travellers see the city before the festivities; the remaining free hours are worth using to rest before a long night.

**New Year's Eve dinner and tickets to a hotel party cost extra.** They are optional and are not part of the group package. This distinction matters: hotel accommodation and excursions are included, but a separate festive dinner on Copacabana is not automatically booked.

On 1 January, the group is scheduled to ascend Sugarloaf Mountain by cable car via Urca. The holiday crowds may require changes to the city-tour order, so avoid adding inflexible, independently booked activities on that date.

## Both sides of Iguazu and the flight into Argentina

At Iguazu, the scenery changes from beachside Rio to humid subtropical forest and powerful waterfalls along an international border. The Brazilian side offers broad views across the cascades; on the Argentine side, via [Puerto Iguazú](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/), walking trails approach the falls and Devil's Throat.

Excursions on both sides are included with a Russian-speaking guide. [Parque das Aves](/brazil/place/parque-das-aves/) and the Macuco Safari boat ride are optional paid activities. Visiting the Argentine side takes place on the same day as the flight to Buenos Aires, so travel planning must allow for the border crossing, airport transfer and flight schedule.

Water levels and weather restrictions can affect access to certain walkways. An excursion to the falls should not be interpreted as a guarantee that every possible trail will be open.

## Buenos Aires and Santiago: two contrasting finales

In [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/), the itinerary includes a guided city tour and a tango show with dinner. This is the cultural section after the lively seaside celebration and the nature excursions at Iguazu. Travellers interested in urban history may particularly enjoy [La Boca](/argentina/place/la-boca/) and San Telmo, but independent additions need to fit the brief two-night stop.

In Chile, the tour covers central neighbourhoods and Santa Lucía Hill. An optional wine tasting in the [Maipo Valley](/chile/place/maipo-valley/) costs **$230 per person with a minimum of two participants**. This is an option for those wishing to end the trip with a culinary experience; the standard Santiago excursion is already included.

The three central impressions therefore come from different countries: celebration and the ocean in Brazil, tango and the falls in Argentina and the border region, and the cityscape beneath the Andes in Chile. The journey reveals different sides of the continent, but leaves limited free time after transfers.

## Flights, hotels and pricing

The package includes **10 hotel nights in the selected category**, group transfers, main excursions with Russian-speaking guides, and flights **Rio–Iguazu–Buenos Aires–Santiago**. International travel to Rio and home from Chile costs extra. Meals are limited to breakfasts and the services expressly included in the chosen programme; the tango dinner is included, but New Year's Eve dinner is not.

The starting price is **from $5,008 per person**, based on three travellers sharing a TPL room in 3-star hotels. Other rates are offered for SGL, DBL and TPL occupancy and 3-, 4- and 5-star hotel categories. When comparing prices, check hotel category, room occupancy and service inclusions rather than just the lowest advertised amount.

Pack light clothing for warm, humid Rio together with comfortable shoes and rain protection for Iguazu; a separate layer may be useful on cool evenings in Santiago. For cross-border flights, check the document requirements for your nationality, any transit rules and baggage allowances on the chosen services.

## How this tour differs from the February carnival

The New Year programme is built around **31 December on Copacabana**. If the samba schools' spectacle at the Sambadrome interests you more, we offer a separate [2027 Champions' Parade tour](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-chile-champions-parade-10-days-2027/). The dates and events differ; a celebration in Rio does not automatically include tickets to the carnival parade.

For other journeys linked to particular dates, explore [Events and Festivals](/interests/events-and-festivals/).

## Frequently asked questions about the New Year journey

### Is the festive dinner on 31 December included?

No. New Year's Eve dinner or a separate hotel party on Copacabana is optional. The basic package includes accommodation, excursions and a tango show with dinner in Buenos Aires.

### Do I need to purchase flights between the countries myself?

The Rio–Iguazu–Buenos Aires–Santiago flights are included. International flights to the starting point and home are paid separately.

### Can I add a boat excursion at the waterfalls?

Yes. Macuco Safari and Parque das Aves are optional paid activities. Their timing and availability must be coordinated with the main Iguazu programme and the onward flight.

### How much time is available to relax in Rio after New Year?

2 January is an entirely free day. Sugarloaf Mountain and a city tour are scheduled for 1 January, so there are not two consecutive free days after New Year's Eve.

## New Year 2027 in Brazil, Argentina and Chile: how the 10-day tour works

From **30 December 2026 to 8 January 2027**, the journey combines three countries and four stops: [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/), [Foz do Iguaçu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/), [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/) and [Santiago de Chile](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/). Over 10 days and nine nights, travellers spend New Year's Eve on Copacabana, explore the falls from both sides of the border and discover the capitals of Argentina and Chile.

The order of stops is especially important here. The celebration takes place at the start, after the group has already arrived in Rio; a nature section at Iguazu and two city stops follow. On such a busy itinerary, it helps to know how much time is allocated to each place and where flights are required.

## Where the nine nights are spent

| Stop | Nights and main purpose |
| --- | --- |
| Rio de Janeiro | 3 nights; New Year and the main viewpoints |
| Foz do Iguaçu | 2 nights; Brazilian and Argentine waterfalls |
| Buenos Aires | 2 nights; city tour and tango |
| Santiago de Chile | 2 nights; Chilean capital and journey's end |

**Flights Rio–Iguazu–Buenos Aires–Santiago are included in the programme.** When comparing this tour's price with others, check the actual air travel included and not simply the number of days.

## Celebrating New Year: why the trip begins in Rio

On 30 December, participants arrive in [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/) and check into their hotel. The next day includes an excursion to Christ the Redeemer on Corcovado, followed by New Year's Eve on Copacabana beach. This is the itinerary's main festive highlight.

Rio's Réveillon celebrations traditionally feature white clothing, concerts by the sea and fireworks above the water. Copacabana can be extremely crowded on New Year's Eve. Agree on a meeting point, how to return to the hotel and when to head towards the beach in advance. **A New Year's Eve dinner or hotel party is offered separately** and is not a compulsory part of the included package.

On 1 January, Sugarloaf Mountain and a Rio sightseeing tour are scheduled. The programme expressly allows changes to the order of visits during the holiday period. Travellers seeking several free beach days in Rio should compare longer [Brazil tours](/brazil/tour/).

## Iguazu: how the two sides of the border differ

After flying to the Iguazu region, travellers visit the Brazilian and Argentine parts of the waterfalls separately. From [Foz do Iguaçu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/), the route follows the canyon and offers broad views of many cascades at once. On the Argentine side near [Puerto Iguazú](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/), walkways lead above and closer to the water; the itinerary includes the Lower and Upper Circuits and Devil's Throat.

These are two contrasting ways of seeing the same natural complex. Rather than repeating one viewpoint, the route offers both sweeping panoramas and an experience closer to the waterfalls. Comfortable shoes, protection for belongings against spray and readiness for humid heat are important. Access to individual bridges depends on park conditions and water levels.

Crossing the Brazil–Argentina border requires checking entry documents for the traveller's nationality. Even a short visit to the other side of the falls involves entering another country. Ada Tours helps coordinate these formalities with the excursions and onward flight to Buenos Aires.

On the day visiting the Brazilian falls, optional activities such as Macuco Safari and the Bird Park may be added for an extra fee.

## From tango to the Andes: finishing in Argentina and Chile

In [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/), the itinerary includes historic neighbourhoods, central squares and a tango show. After the nature section at Iguazu, travellers turn to city sightseeing. Two nights are allocated to the capital, making it a good introduction for visitors who are not planning a longer Argentina tour.

Day eight includes a flight to [Santiago](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/). Day nine introduces Chile's capital: Plaza de Armas, historic buildings, Santa Lucía Hill and modern districts. The journey ends on 8 January with a transfer to the airport. Other destinations can be explored through [Chile tours](/chile/tour/) and [Argentina tours](/argentina/tour/).

## What is included and what to budget for separately

The programme includes hotel accommodation, group excursions with Russian-speaking guides, shared transfers with a driver and the listed regional flights. **International flights are excluded.** Optional excursions, meals and drinks outside the programme, tips and laundry are also paid separately.

When comparing offers, confirm the airport of arrival in Rio and departure from Santiago: the journey starts and finishes in different countries. International flights must be selected with attention to both fares and possible connections, transit rules and arrival time before the programme begins.

## Who should choose this version

The 10-day itinerary suits those whose principal event is **New Year on Copacabana**, followed by both sides of Iguazu and two South American capitals without a lengthy high-altitude section.

If you want to continue via Bolivia and Peru, compare the [19-day New Year journey through five countries](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-new-year-group-tour-19-days/). It is considerably longer and includes the Altiplano, Uyuni and Machu Picchu. For Chile's desert and highland lagoons, [Sun, Tango, Wine and Atacama](/multi-country/tour/sun-tango-wine-atacama/) has a different itinerary and different flight inclusions.

## Frequently asked questions about the 2027 New Year tour

### Where do travellers celebrate New Year?

On Copacabana in Rio de Janeiro on the evening of 31 December 2026. A separate dinner or hotel party can be arranged at extra cost.

### Can I see Iguazu from both Brazil and Argentina?

Yes. The approved itinerary includes both visits on different days, with a crossing of the international border.

### Are flights between the countries included?

The listed regional flights Rio–Iguazu–Buenos Aires–Santiago are included. International flights to and from the journey cost extra.

### Do I have to book optional excursions?

No. Macuco Safari, the Bird Park and separate festive offers are optional. Their availability can be discussed according to free time and your interests.

## Brazil, Argentina, Chile and Peru in 15 days: four distinct stages

This four-country itinerary combines [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/), both sides of Iguazu Falls, [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/), [Santiago de Chile](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/) and Peru's Inca heritage sites. Over **15 days and 14 nights**, the journey gradually moves from the ocean and major cities to the [Sacred Valley](/peru/place/sacred-valley-of-the-incas/), [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/) and [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/).

The key reason to add Peru is **several days dedicated to history and archaeology**, rather than one more brief airport stop. This programme suits travellers who want to experience several different countries while setting aside a substantial section for Inca heritage.

## How this itinerary differs from the three-country tour

The first section resembles the [12-day Brazil, Argentina and Chile tour](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-chile-iguazu-12-days/): [Rio](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/) with Corcovado and Sugarloaf, [Iguazu on the Brazilian](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/) and [Argentine sides](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/), [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/) and [Santiago](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/).

The difference begins after Chile. Rather than ending in Santiago, travellers fly to Peru. Here the programme includes the [Sacred Valley of the Incas](/peru/place/sacred-valley-of-the-incas/), [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/), cultural and historical visits in Cusco, and an ending in [Lima](/peru/place/lima/).

Extending the journey from 12 to 15 days does not mean three extra free days. Peru is packed with travel and sightseeing, so independent walks and rest should be planned around the actual schedule.

## Iguazu and Buenos Aires: more than stops between flights

At [Iguazu Falls](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/), a dedicated day is scheduled on the Brazilian side. The route then crosses the border to the [Argentine cascades](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/) before continuing to Buenos Aires. This allows visitors to compare Brazil's sweeping views with the close-up experience on the Argentine walkways.

[Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/) includes a city tour and some free time, providing a break between busy stages. If you want to add a private excursion or a culinary experience, compare the available hours with the flight to Santiago.

## Chile: Santiago and a visit to the Pacific coast

Chile's main city stop is [Santiago de Chile](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/). The itinerary includes a journey to [Valparaíso and Viña del Mar](/chile/place/valparaiso-vina-del-mar/). These cities introduce the Pacific coastline before the climate and altitude change in Peru.

Valparaíso is known for its historic harbour and steep hillside neighbourhoods. The coast is part of the tour, not a separate optional country: Chile is a full stage of the main itinerary. An onward flight to Peru follows, and the total number of flight segments becomes an important factor in calculating the full cost.

## Peru: why the Sacred Valley has several dedicated days

The most substantial Peru stage takes place in the [Sacred Valley of the Incas](/peru/place/sacred-valley-of-the-incas/). Stops include [Pisac](/peru/place/pisac/), [Ollantaytambo](/peru/place/ollantaytambo/), [Chinchero](/peru/place/chinchero/), [Moray](/peru/place/moray/) and Awanakancha. These separate stops reveal the valley's archaeological sites and communities rather than reducing Peru to a single famous photograph of Machu Picchu.

The [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/) excursion uses the **Vistadome train**; the train ticket and entrance tickets are included in the tour. The route then continues via [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/) to [Lima](/peru/place/lima/).

On the final day before departure, you explore Lima: the Main Square and cathedral, San Francisco Monastery and the San Isidro and Miraflores districts. After the tour, you return to the hotel and transfer to the airport.

Altitude, transfers and early departures in Peru can be more demanding than a routine city excursion. Pack and pace the journey for mountain conditions and individual health considerations. This itinerary **does not include the Bolivia expedition across Uyuni** that features on some five-country tours.

## Included services and separate expenses

The package includes **14 hotel nights with breakfasts**, transfers and excursions along the route, admission tickets and the Vistadome train ticket to Machu Picchu.

However, **regional flights are excluded from the price**. The sequence Rio–Iguazu–Buenos Aires–Santiago–Cusco–Lima is paid separately. International flights, optional excursions, and food and drinks during transfers are also excluded. Compare this tour against neighbouring multi-country programmes by adding flight segments where another offer already includes them.

Check the actual flight routing as well: the journey finishes in Lima, and the connection to Cusco is essential to the Peru section.

## When to choose 15 days instead of 12 or 18

The **15-day version** is for travellers who value Machu Picchu and the Sacred Valley as much as Rio, Iguazu and Buenos Aires. If Peru is optional, the [12-day itinerary with Chile and Iguazu](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-chile-iguazu-12-days/) offers a shorter geographic route and included regional flights.

If you also want Bolivia's high-altitude lagoons, Uyuni Salt Flat and Lake Titicaca, consider the [18-day group itinerary through five countries](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-group-tour-18-days/). Its climate and transfers are more demanding, but it adds a very different natural region.

## Frequently asked questions about the four-country tour

### Does the tour include Machu Picchu and the Sacred Valley?

Yes. The Peru programme covers the valley with several historic stops, the train to Machu Picchu and a visit to Cusco.

### Are regional flights included in the price?

No. They are listed as a separate expense, although transfers, main excursions and admission tickets are included.

### Is the train ticket to Machu Picchu included?

Yes. The price includes the Vistadome train ticket to Machu Picchu.

### Why does a four-country journey last 15 days?

Because it adds a dedicated Peru section with the Sacred Valley, Machu Picchu, Cusco and Lima, while several flights between the regions are still required.

## Chile, Argentina, Uruguay and Brazil in 17 days: how the route works

This **17-day, 16-night** journey starts in [Santiago de Chile](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/). It then passes through Chilean and Argentine Patagonia, [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/), a day visit to [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/), Iguazu Falls and [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/). The final days are dedicated to the beaches of [Búzios](/brazil/place/buzios/).

Unlike itineraries on which Uruguay is merely an optional excursion, **Montevideo is part of the planned main route**. The four countries complement each other with southern mountains and glaciers, historic capital districts, subtropical waterfalls and time beside the Atlantic.

## What happens in each country

| Country | Main stage |
|---|---|
| Chile | Santiago, Torres del Paine |
| Argentina | Perito Moreno, Buenos Aires |
| Uruguay | Day trip to Montevideo |
| Brazil | Iguazu, Rio, Búzios |

The Chile section begins with Santiago, then heads south to [Puerto Natales and Torres del Paine](/chile/place/puerto-natales-torres-del-paine/). Mountains, lakes, valleys and forests call for warm clothing and preparation for wind, even in favourable seasons. A sightseeing visit to the park does not entail a compulsory demanding multi-day trekking route.

From Puerto Natales, the journey continues by bus to [El Calafate](/argentina/place/el-calafate/) across the Chile–Argentina border. The next natural attraction is [Perito Moreno Glacier](/argentina/place/perito-moreno-glacier/) with its viewing platforms. Passport formalities and the timing of the overland crossing matter; this is not an ordinary domestic transfer.

In Buenos Aires, the programme includes a city tour, an evening tango show and a separate "Fiesta Gaucha" ranch experience. A ferry then takes travellers across the Río de la Plata to Montevideo and back. This is an actual **visit to another country**, requiring attention to entry into Uruguay and re-entry into Argentina.

The route next heads to the waterfalls. On the [Puerto Iguazú side](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/), travellers explore national park walkways; on the [Foz do Iguaçu side](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/), they enjoy wide panoramas across the cascades. After flying to Rio, the itinerary includes Corcovado, Sugarloaf Mountain and the historic centre, followed by two full beach days in Búzios.

## Why flights and border crossings need time buffers

Over 17 days, several types of transport are used: regional flights, a bus between the two sides of Patagonia, a ferry excursion to Montevideo, a border crossing at Iguazu and an overland transfer from Rio to the coastal resort. The sequence **Chile → Argentina → Uruguay → Argentina → Brazil** must be coordinated with the passengers' actual tickets and documents.

Each country has its own entry and stay rules, and transit requirements depend on nationality and flight routes. There is no automatic universal "South American visa" for this journey. We can help coordinate connections and identify which documents and crossings must be checked before booking, but the applicable national rules determine the final conditions.

The through-route logistics matter more than the lines drawn on a map: even a minor flight delay in Patagonia can affect a bus border crossing or the next hotel. Add optional excursions on transfer days only once the tickets are confirmed.

## How the weather and physical demands differ

Torres del Paine and Perito Moreno require warm layers, waterproof protection and shoes suitable for viewing trails. Chile's CONAF publishes rules for authorised trails and alerts about temporary restrictions. At Iguazu, expect heat, humidity and spray; Búzios requires beachwear and sun protection.

Pack for two different environments: the mountainous south and the warm lowlands. Baggage allowances of the particular carriers also matter at borders and on domestic flights. Assess medical limitations for individual activities and the ability to manage long walks before choosing the tour, particularly for a large group with varying fitness levels.

## Hotels, guides and occupancy rates

The programme provides accommodation in **4-star hotels** with breakfasts, with prices per person for the whole journey. The rates for **2027** depend on room occupancy:

| Occupancy | USD per person |
|---|---:|
| SGL — single | 11,957 |
| DBL — double | 6,836 |
| TRP — triple | 6,227 |

Included are accommodation with breakfasts, main excursions, private transfers and the specified admission tickets. **Russian-speaking guides** are provided in Rio, Iguazu and Buenos Aires. Fiesta Gaucha, Montevideo, Perito Moreno and Torres del Paine excursions take place privately or in a shared group **with English-speaking guides**. This is an important distinction for travellers who require Russian-language guiding on every stage.

**International and regional flights, optional excursions, personal expenses and tips are excluded.** Air tickets must be budgeted separately from the selected SGL/DBL/TRP rate. Some hotel breakfasts may be missed because of early departures, as expressly noted in the programme terms.

## Comparing this journey with shorter options

The 17-day tour suits travellers who want four countries with time for both natural parks and the ocean. For a shorter trip, consider the [10-day Argentina–Brazil itinerary including Perito Moreno and Iguazu](/multi-country/tour/best-of-argentina-brazil-10-days/), without Chile, Uruguay and a separate beach finale. Alternatively, focus on two countries and beaches: the [13-day Peru and Brazil programme](/multi-country/tour/peru-machu-picchu-brazil-rio-beaches/) features Machu Picchu and Titicaca instead of southern Patagonia.

The main question is whether you are ready for several border formalities and transfers in exchange for four very different sections of the continent. If the goal is only a glacier or only the ocean, a more focused journey usually leaves more free time.

## Frequently asked questions about the four-country tour

### Is Uruguay really included in the itinerary?

Yes. A ferry excursion to Montevideo is scheduled for day ten. It is included as a separate visit to the country.

### Are all the guides Russian-speaking?

No. Russian-speaking guides are specified for Rio, Iguazu and Buenos Aires. English-speaking guides are specified for Patagonia, Fiesta Gaucha and Montevideo.

### What does the $6,836 price include?

This is the **DBL rate** per person for the programme with two people sharing a room. Four-star hotels, breakfasts, main excursions, transfers and admission tickets are included; international and regional flights cost extra.

### Are there days to relax beside the ocean?

Yes. After Rio, the programme includes two days in Búzios, followed by a return to Rio airport for the flight home.
